Package io.thymekit

Class Element.Descriptor<K>

java.lang.Object
io.thymekit.Element.Descriptor<K>
All Implemented Interfaces:
Composable<K>
Enclosing class:
Element<K>
public static final class Element.Descriptor<K> extends Object implements Composable<K>
Builds a descriptor: adapter address plus data, terminal build(). It becomes an element, and says so — a descriptor goes into a page or a slot exactly where an element goes.

  • Method Details

    • of

      public static <K> Element.Descriptor<K> of(String template, String fragment)
      Entry point for an element factory — its own adapter address and marker: Element.Descriptor.<MyCard>of("fragments/my/card", "myCardEl").with(…).build(). Elements are written this way both inside the kit and in consumer code.

    • with

      public Element.Descriptor<K> with(String key, Object value)
      Element data; the adapter reads it as ${e['key']}. Reserved keys are rejected.

      A collection handed in here is copied, however deep it goes. An element is its descriptor — that is what makes two of them equal and what asset deduplication counts on — so a list the caller still holds must not be able to change the element after it was built.

    • describes

      public Element.Descriptor<K> describes(Map<String,?> node)
      What this element says about itself for machines — a JSON-LD node, as data. The canvas collects the contributions of a page, turns them into text once and prints one block; an element never prints its own, and never carries finished text, because a descriptor holding markup is the one seam through which markup could reach a page that was stored rather than composed.

      What may be in it is what the kit can write: text, whole numbers, true or false, maps and lists. Anything else is refused here, not when a page is rendered, and the refusal names the path that reaches it.

      One element describes itself once. A second call is a mistake either way — accumulating would guess at what was meant, replacing would lose the first quietly — so it is refused.

    • slot

      public Element.Descriptor<K> slot(String name, List<? extends Composable<?>> items)
      A named slot of a composite element. What may go in is constrained by the factory's slot method, not here; an empty list leaves the slot unrendered.
